title: Normalization and the gluing-parameter sequence of a nodal curve
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], and let $C/\Omega$ be a proper connected reduced nodal curve [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $
u:\coprod_{i\in I}\widetilde C_i	o C$ be its normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], indexed by the finite set of irreducible components. Each $\widetilde C_i$ is a smooth projective connected curve. Let $E$ be the finite set of nodes, choose an ordering of the two preimages of each node, and let $i_-(e),i_+(e)\in I$ be the components containing them. Put $P_C=\operatorname{Pic}_{C/\Omega}$ and $P_i=\operatorname{Pic}_{\widetilde C_i/\Omega}$ [sk-def-picard-pic]. There is an exact sequence of fppf sheaves of commutative groups on $\Omega$-schemes
$$1\longrightarrow\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\mathrm{diag}}\mathbf G_m^I\xrightarrow{\delta}\mathbf G_m^E\longrightarrow P_C\xrightarrow{
u^*}\prod_{i\in I}P_i\longrightarrow0,\qquad \delta((a_i))_e=a_{i_+(e)}a_{i_-(e)}^{-1}.$$
Here $\mathbf G_m(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^	imes$. The map $\mathbf G_m^E	o P_C$ assigns gluing parameters to the trivial line modules on the components. Let $J_i\subset P_i$ be the degree-zero Jacobian [def-sc-jacobian], and put $B=\prod_iJ_i$. Then $B$ is an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. The sheaf $Q=\operatorname{coker}\delta$ is represented by an algebraic group, and the inverse image $D_C=(
u^*)^{-1}(B)$ is represented by a smooth group algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]; the induced map $D_C	o B$ is a smooth surjective open $Q$-torsor. A $Q$-torsor here means a sheaf with a $Q$-action which becomes the translation action of $Q$ on itself after an fppf covering. These statements concern the sheaves on all $\Omega$-schemes, not only their $\Omega$-points.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-completed-normalization-model] to $C$: its hypotheses hold because a nodal curve is nonempty and pure one-dimensional, reduced and proper, with completed node rings $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. It gives finite $E$, finite normalization and the smooth projective connected components asserted. At a node $e$, write $A=\mathcal O_{C,e}$ and $A^
u=(
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C})_e$. The residue difference $A^
u	o\Omega$, $b\mapsto b(e_+)-b(e_-)$, gives a complex $0	o A	o A^
u	o\Omega	o0$. After tensoring with $\widehat A$, the cited completed model makes this the exact sequence of pairs of power series and their constant-term difference. The completion is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]; flat tensor exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] and reflection of zero modules [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero], applied to the kernel and cokernel defects, show that the original complex is exact. Away from $E$, normalization is an isomorphism. Thus $\mathcal O_C$ is the subsheaf of normalized functions whose two values agree at each node. Set $Z=\coprod_E\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $Z'=\coprod_E(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\amalg\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$. The same local computation gives $Z'=\widetilde C	imes_C Z$ scheme-theoretically: $\mathfrak m_eA^
u$ equals the ideal of the two reduced points, since this equality holds after completion and its quotient is detected by faithful flatness. Consequently this is an affine fibre-product square with $\mathcal O_C=
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C}	imes_{\mathcal O_{Z'}}\mathcal O_Z$.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, with Example 0C1J (example-glue-points); relative argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text: Every $\Omega$-scheme is flat over $\Omega$. Tensoring the affine ring sequences of Step 1 with a $\Omega$-algebra preserves exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], so the same fibre-product square holds over every $T$, including nonreduced $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-pinching-invertible-patching]. A line bundle on $C_T$ is a line bundle $L_i$ on each $\widetilde C_i\times T$, a line bundle $N_e$ on each node copy of $T$, and identifications $L_{i_-(e)}|_{e_-}\simeq N_e\simeq L_{i_+(e)}|_{e_+}$. Eliminating $N_e$ gives exactly one branch identification $\lambda_e:L_{i_-(e)}|_{e_-}\to L_{i_+(e)}|_{e_+}$ per node, and morphisms are component isomorphisms commuting with these identifications. Conversely take $N_e=L_{i_-(e)}|_{e_-}$ to reconstruct the triple. These operations are inverse up to the indicated isomorphisms, respect tensor products and commute with base change by the cited patching equivalence. In particular arbitrary gluing units on trivial $L_i$ define a homomorphism $\mathbf G_m^E\to P_C$.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, with Example 0C1J (example-glue-points); relative argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text: Each $\widetilde C_i$ is a nonempty smooth connected one-dimensional curve; [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] makes it integral. By properness, [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] says $H^0(\widetilde C_i,\mathcal O)$ is a finite field extension of $\Omega$, hence is $\Omega$ because $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. Flat base change [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom], in degree zero over any affine $T$, gives $(\mathrm{pr}_T)_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C_i\times T}=\mathcal O_T$. These identifications glue on arbitrary $T$, so automorphisms of the trivial component bundles are exactly $\mathbf G_m(T)^I$. Changing their frames by $(a_i)$ sends $\lambda_e$ to $a_{i_+(e)}\lambda_ea_{i_-(e)}^{-1}$. Thus a trivial-component gluing is isomorphic to the trivial gluing precisely when its parameters lie in $\operatorname{im}\delta$. The dual graph is connected: a partition of its vertices with no crossing edge would partition the finite set of irreducible components of $C$ into two disjoint closed unions, contradicting connectedness. Therefore $\ker\delta$ consists exactly of tuples with all $a_i$ equal, on every $T$; this is the diagonal copy of $\mathbf G_m$.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, with Example 0C1J (example-glue-points); relative argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text:
Use the sheafification definition [sk-def-picard-pic]. A section of $\prod_iP_i$ is fppf locally represented by bundles $L_i$. There are finitely many branches; their restricted line bundles on $T$ become trivial on a common Zariski cover. On that cover choose the $\lambda_e$ and glue by Step 2. Hence $
u^*$ is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves. A section of $P_C$ whose pullback is zero is locally represented by $L$ with every $
u_i^*L$ trivial: first choose representatives, then refine where their zero classes become trivial bundles, as allowed by sheafification. Step 2 then expresses $L$ by gluing units. Likewise if such a gluing has zero class in $P_C$, refine so its bundle is trivial, and Step 3 expresses its parameters as $\delta((a_i))$. These arguments also account for bundles pulled back from $T$, since they are Zariski locally trivial. Thus the sequence in the statement is exact as sheaves on all $\Omega$-schemes. In particular $\ker(
u^*)=Q=\operatorname{coker}\delta$.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, with Example 0C1J (example-glue-points); relative argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text: Choose a root vertex and a spanning tree $F$ in the connected finite dual graph by adjoining, until all vertices occur, an edge from a reached vertex to an unreached vertex. For parameters $\lambda\in\mathbf G_m(T)^E$, set $a_{\rm root}=1$ and recursively choose the other $a_i$ so that $(\delta(a)\lambda)_e=1$ on every tree edge: if $e$ points from parent $p$ to child $c$, take $a_c=a_p\lambda_e^{-1}$; if it points the other way, take $a_c=a_p\lambda_e$. Each $a_i$ is a Laurent monomial in tree parameters. This normalization is unique, since a tuple in $\operatorname{im}\delta$ which is $1$ on all tree edges is $1$ everywhere. The remaining parameters on $E\setminus F$ therefore give a natural group isomorphism $Q\simeq\mathbf G_m^{E\setminus F}$, with inverse induced by assigning $1$ on $F$. It is defined on arbitrary test schemes by the same Laurent monomials. The representing scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t_e^{\pm1}:e\in E\setminus F]$; multiplication and inverse are coordinatewise and hence it is an algebraic group. Its smoothness follows from [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with the free lattice on $E\setminus F$. For a smooth connected curve $E=\varnothing$ and $I$ is a singleton; for a tree $Q=1$; a self-node is a non-tree edge and contributes one unrestricted factor.

source.place: Tag 0C1M (lemma-glue-points), units-sequence proof, with Example 0C1J (example-glue-points); relative argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-picard-main] to each smooth proper connected $\widetilde C_i$. Its degree-zero Picard sheaf $J_i$ is represented by a smooth proper geometrically connected commutative group scheme. The product scheme $B=\prod_iJ_i$ represents their product functor, with coordinatewise group law. It is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], and smooth by base change and composition in [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (the relative dimensions of the factors are their genera). It is connected by induction using [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components]. Thus [def-sc-abelian-variety] identifies $B$ as an abelian variety.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), degree-zero component, and finite products; product permanence uses the cited nodes.

proof.text: Pull back the epimorphism $P_C\to\prod_iP_i$ along $B\hookrightarrow\prod_iP_i$. This gives $D_C\to B$, with kernel $Q$. For two sections of $D_C$ over a common section of $B$, their difference is a unique section of $Q$ by Step 4. Consequently $Q\times D_C\to D_C\times_BD_C$, $(q,d)\mapsto(q+d,d)$, is an isomorphism of sheaves. The epimorphism supplies fppf local sections; translating by one identifies the pullback of $D_C$ with $Q\times B$. Thus this is precisely the torsor required in the statement. Since $Q$ is the smooth affine finitely presented split torus of Step 5 and $B$ is a scheme, [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-group-torsor-representability] represents $D_C$ by a scheme, affine smooth surjective and open over $B$. The composite with $B\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition], because $B$ is smooth. The sheaf's group operations are morphisms of the representing scheme by Yoneda. A scheme is in particular an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], so this gives the asserted smooth group algebraic space and its smooth surjective open $Q$-torsor map.
